quiz.title: Composition & Inverse Functions Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on gof, fog, one-one, onto and finding inverses, straight from Exercise 1.3. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Relations and Functions, Exercise 1.3

questions.q: If f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 3, what is (gof)(x)?
questions.explanation: (gof)(x) = g(f(x)) = g(2x) = 2x + 3. Apply f first, then g.

questions.q: For the same f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 3, what is (fog)(x)?
questions.explanation: (fog)(x) = f(g(x)) = f(x + 3) = 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6. Notice fog is not the same as gof.

questions.q: A function f is invertible if and only if it is:
questions.explanation: A function has an inverse exactly when it is a bijection, that is one-one (injective) and onto (surjective) together.

questions.q: If f(x) = 3x + 5 on R, what is its inverse f-inverse(y)?
questions.explanation: Set y = 3x + 5, so x = (y - 5)/3. Hence f-inverse(y) = (y - 5)/3.

questions.q: If f is invertible, then (f-inverse o f)(x) equals:
questions.explanation: Composing a function with its inverse gives the identity: (f-inverse o f)(x) = x for every x in the domain.

questions.q: If f: R to R is f(x) = x squared, why is it NOT invertible?
questions.explanation: f(2) = f(-2) = 4, so different inputs share an output. It fails the one-one test, so no inverse exists on all of R.

questions.q: If (gof) is onto, which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The final output of gof comes from g, so if gof is onto then g must be onto. f need not be onto.

questions.q: For invertible f and g, the inverse of (gof) is:
questions.explanation: The reversal law gives (gof)-inverse = f-inverse o g-inverse. Undo the last-applied function (g) first.

faq.q: What does Exercise 1.3 of Class 12 Relations and Functions cover?
faq.a: It deals with composition of functions (gof and fog) and invertible functions. You learn to compute composites, check whether a function is one-one and onto, and find the inverse when it exists.

faq.q: Is gof the same as fog?
faq.a: Usually not. gof means apply f first then g, while fog applies g first then f. For f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 3 you get gof = 2x + 3 but fog = 2x + 6, so the order genuinely matters.
A function is invertible exactly when it is a bijection — both one-one (injective) and onto (surjective). If either property fails, no inverse exists over that domain and codomain.

faq.q: How do I find the inverse of a function?
faq.a: First confirm it is one-one and onto. Then write y = f(x), solve the equation for x in terms of y, and swap the roles so f-inverse(y) is that expression. For f(x) = 3x + 5 you get f-inverse(y) = (y - 5)/3.
